name: Inventurus Knowledge Solutions Ltd
title: Inventurus Knowledge Solutions Ltd - 544309 -  Announcement Under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Conference Call Transcript

read.thesis: Transformational debt-funded acquisition of TruBridge (EV ~$557m, ~3x EBITDA on $69m adjusted EBITDA) to take IKS into US RCM and EHR; no supply-side or capacity signal, and management declined to quantify synergies.

guidance.quote: if by the end of FY30 not delivered

summary.headline: IKS agreed to acquire TruBridge for ~$557M enterprise value (~3x EBITDA), funded by $565M debt; management guides to ~INR3,000 crore revenue ambition by FY30.
summary.overview: IKS signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire TruBridge, a US listed EHR and RCM provider, on April 23, 2026, with closing expected in 90 to 120 days subject to HSR/FTC clearance. TruBridge's trailing CY2025 revenue was $347M ($126M EHR, $221M RCM) and adjusted EBITDA was $69M, versus $186M-plus on a reported-to-adjusted basis cited by management. Management framed the deal as adding an EHR installed base of about 700 clients as a distribution and data moat for IKS's AI-led RCM and clinical workflow platform. The call focused on strategic rationale and TAM, with limited detail on synergy quantum or timing beyond G&A-first sequencing and a four-year timeline.

financial_highlights.change: Equity value $427M; net debt assumed about $130M as of March 31
Reported EBITDA $159M; management-adjusted figure cited as $186M on $698M revenue basis, after removing ESOP ($43M), public-company and one-time costs ($9.5M and others)
5-year term loan at SOFR+275 bps, stepping down to SOFR+175 bps as leverage falls; starting leverage ~3x EBITDA
Management said instantly EPS and PAT accretive; analyst noted a $12M amortisation item not included in the calculation

financial_highlights.value: INR1,000 crore gross cash, net cash INR300 crore

segments.name: TruBridge RCM
segments.commentary: CY2025 RCM revenue $221M; management estimates about 30% of TruBridge's ~700 EHR clients (about $220M RCM spend) already outsource RCM, leaving a white space of roughly $450M.

segments.name: TruBridge EHR
segments.commentary: CY2025 EHR revenue $126M; roughly 2,200 hospitals in the US, with ~700 clients in the 0-50 bed segment where penetration is about 40%, and about 30% penetration across the broader base.

segments.name: TruCode (encoder)
segments.commentary: Management cited a $650M TAM for the encoder tool, which is sold stand-alone; competitors named are 3M and Optum.

segments.name: IKS base business
segments.commentary: IKS has ~17,000 people (2,000 clinically trained, 800-plus technologists); 8 of its 18 service lines are technology-led; the RCM programme ran at about $220M-equivalent spend on about 3,500 FTEs globally in the cited comparison.

guidance_outlook: Management's FY30 north star: about INR3,000 crore revenue (from INR1,000 crore base), a ~31% CAGR from Dec 2025 to Mar 2030; explicitly not formal guidance, with a stated fallback that if not achieved, net debt would be reduced to zero.
Management will not change its aspirations to grow faster than the ~12% US industry rate; it expects to be fairly confident on margin but less certain on growth over 2-3 years.

Synergy timing: G&A synergies first (Q1 post-close learning, Q2 actioning single organisation structure); operational synergies from Q3 post-close; management expects the transformation to take 4-5 years.
Deal closing expected in 90-120 days, subject to HSR approval from the FTC.

Management said the combined TAM for the RCM outsourced market is $3.5-4B against about $1B outsourced today, with serviceable immediate TAM of about $660M (2% take rate on 700-client base of $32B revenue).
capex_capacity: Plan to migrate TruBridge EHR to a cloud-native, AI-first architecture; management believes this will allow penetration of 0-50 bed hospitals and gradual upstream move into 50-200 bed range.
Small language models (SLMs) sitting on top of LLMs are planned to reduce compute and build proprietary self-learning loops for RCM.
Acute RCM offering to be launched; Scribble ambient scribing product to be upgraded into a live encounter co-pilot.
Management described the EHR modernisation as costly for TruBridge, previously a drain on financials, and said IKS would bring agile, cost-optimised development.
demand_pricing: RCM is fragmented: top players hold under 20% share, with 400-plus players and a long tail; US healthcare RCM spend about $1.75-1.8 trillion, of which management's modelled addressable base is around 2% take rate.
Management modelled 2% take rate for RCM outsourcing (versus about 3% today) to conservatively allow for price compression from AI.

Competitors named: Med-Metrix and CorroHealth (RCM BPO); 3M and Optum (encoders); Epic, Athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen (EHR); Oracle Cerner challenger; MEDITECH; Phreesia, Augmedix, Abridge, Ambience and Microsoft DAX in ambient AI.
Management argues outcome-based pricing will replace per-user SaaS pricing as AI orchestrates tasks; TruBridge's 700-client base is outpatient-heavy (60-70% of volume).
Management said the parent's own attempts at globalising RCM and building a captive in India had not succeeded, and that IKS brings an offshore-enabled model.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition in EHR and RCM, and do IKS's learnings help win the segment? Any overlap between RCM and EHR clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EHR is a two-player market with Epic and Oracle Cerner dominant and MEDITECH a challenger; RCM is largely unmanaged, and about 230-240 of TruBridge's ~700 EHR clients already buy RCM, leaving a large white space. The 500-odd clients without RCM and 1,500 non-TruBridge EHR clients are targets.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the initial synergies or the financial outcome of the merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify synergies beyond saying the INR1,000 crore to INR3,000 crore north star is a definition of success, and said the target contains uncertainty for learnings and mistakes; drivers are RCM transformation, globalisation and G&A, with 2,000-plus RCM FTEs in India versus about 1,000 in US.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the deal structured with a 4-year timeline and why is the organic path hard?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said synergy timing is not being given in detail; G&A synergies come first and operational synergies later; organic growth to 700 clients would take about a decade and IKS's global RCM model is a differentiator given earlier failed attempts.

qa_highlights.question: What are the steps post-close and how will IKS retain customers and talent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management outlined Q1 learning, Q2 actioning new structure, Q3 operational synergies; customer retention was called the gold mine of the transaction, along with identifying and retaining key talent in the first quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How does TruBridge's headcount and RCM proposition compare with IKS's model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EHR has low marginal cost and RCM is tech-led and AI-first; RCM spend at large systems runs about 4-5% of revenue and about 7-10% at hospitals, strengthening the outsourcing proposition.

qa_highlights.question: Does IKS plan to compete with the large EHR vendors at scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is not to take EHR to larger hospitals; EHR is for the 0-50 bed segment, with the 50-200 bed range a later addition, and EHR is to be a sticky source of data for RCM.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth guidance change after closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not changing aspirations of growing faster than the ~12% industry rate, and is less certain on growth than margins over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT accretion of about $5M excluding a $12M amortisation item?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intangible amortisation schedule is being separately evaluated for EHR and RCM relationships, with new asset lives under valuation by experts; the $5M accretion was presented as the highest-possible level, with minor changes possible.

risks_watch: Integration complexity: management says TruBridge's 700-client EHR base was previously a drain; execution of modernisation to cloud/AI architecture is unproven.
Leverage: $565M debt at SOFR+275 bps; deleveraging depends on internal accruals and EBITDA delivery; management said the 3x starting leverage is higher than it would like.
Regulatory: HSR/FTC review pending; closing in 90-120 days.
Client retention: management flagged customer and talent retention as key priorities; a differentiated integration playbook is still being formed.
AI pricing: shift from per-user SaaS to outcome-based pricing and the 2% RCM take-rate assumption (versus ~3% today) are key model inputs to monitor.
Reported vs adjusted EBITDA gap (CY2025 $159M reported vs $186M adjusted vs $69M cited elsewhere as the adjusted figure) needs reconciliation before valuation work.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on strategy and TAM, but deliberately cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly declined to quantify synergies, called the INR3,000 crore figure a north star rather than guidance, and stressed uncertainty in integration.

growth.why: Management guides to a ~INR3,000 crore FY30 revenue north star (~31% CAGR from INR1,000 crore base, explicitly not formal guidance) and 2-3x industry growth (~12%), backed by the TruBridge acquisition ($557M EV, $565M debt) and TAM claims, but with no specific capacity, orders or contracts with numbers and timing behind the growth.
